correctness.rationale: Every update weakly increases cut size, because the closed-minority flip criterion is \(2s\ge d\) and the cut gain is \(2s-d\). Private clique blades at fixed hub strictly improve until their exact central count levels; those levels jointly attain the sum of the individual clique maximum cuts. An explicit private-only path reaches this closed set. The hub flips in that set iff all blades have even private sizes and are at their upper Boolean level; an odd private-size blade makes the hub inert. Each even blade has a connected adjacent-level inclusion graph, giving all communicating-class counts; every neutral flip reverses with the same \(1/N\) probability, yielding uniform stationarity. For all-even blades, conditional stationary hub-crossing frequency is exactly the product of upper-level proportions divided by N. A density-domination/union-bound argument yields the stated total-variation mixing lower bound without independence assumptions. `check_scc.py` and `check_local.py` were executed from package files and match their recorded outputs, checking 88 entire transition graphs and 637 local/flux tuples. These are finite checks; the proof covers all \(m\ge2\) and \(r_i\ge1\).

value.rationale: Gluing individually simple cliques at an articulation vertex creates a sharp global communication effect: one private vertex added to a blade changes its parity, freezes the hub after recurrence and splits a single irreducible class into \(2\binom{2a+1}{a}\) classes, while the exact number of all recurrent configurations remains unchanged. The result holds for all arbitrary heterogeneous collections of two or more blades and proves global maximum-cut convergence. The exact stationary hub-crossing probability in the all-even case gives a meaningful exponential mixing-time obstruction. These are dynamics/topology invariants and a structural sensitivity phenomenon rather than a mere known clique special case, arbitrary parameter slice or finite enumeration.
